question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)={2}^{x}+1.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5).$
question.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(5),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(5)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(5).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(5)=x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(5) & =x \\ f(x) & =5 \\ {2}^{x}+1 & =5 \\ {2}^{x} & =4 \\ {2}^{x} & ={2}^{2} \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{-1}(5)=2.$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={2}^{x}+1 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{x} \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot {2}^{2} \\ {f}^{′}(2) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(5))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}.\end{aligned}
$$
